test_title: SSC Selection Post 2024 (Higher Secondary Level) Official Paper (Held On: 26 Jun, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Select the option that expresses the following sentence in passive voice.

The reviewer gave a dazzling review of the restaurant, which then went viral.

options.text: A dazzling review of the restaurant was given by the reviewer, which then went viral.
A dazzling review of the restaurant is given by the reviewer, which then went viral.
It went viral when the reviewer gave a dazzling review of the restaurant.
The reviewer was given a dazzling review to the restaurant, which then had gone viral

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In passive voice, the object of an active sentence becomes the subject of the **passive sentence.**
 
• The verb form changes **to accommodate the new subject.**
 
• The phrase** "was given"** correctly converts the active verb **"gave"** into passive form.
 
• The additional clause** "which then went viral"** remains unchanged as it is descriptive.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"**A dazzling review of the restaurant was given by the reviewer, which then went viral."***

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "A dazzling review of the restaurant is given by the reviewer, which then went viral." – This option is incorrect because the verb "is given" is in the present tense, while the original sentence is in the past tense.
 
• **Option 3:** "It went viral when the reviewer gave a dazzling review of the restaurant." – This option is incorrect because it does not express the sentence in passive voice.
 
• **Option 4:** "The reviewer was given a dazzling review to the restaurant, which then had gone viral." – This option is incorrect because it incorrectly places "the reviewer" as the object and uses an incorrect verb form.
